 Two-year tax deadline scrapped for pension death benefits

 It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald.
 A Somerset MP has welcomed a government change that removes a major tax risk for bereaved families.
 Rachel Gilmour, the Liberal Democrat MP for Tiverton and Minehead , said the decision to scrap the two-year deadline for tax-free pension death benefits will bring relief to families who might otherwise face unexpected tax charges due to administrative delays.
 The change applies to beneficiaries of pension scheme members who die before the age of 75.
 Under the previous rules, if the death benefit was not paid within two years of the scheme becoming aware of the death, the payment became taxable.
 Ms Gilmour, a member of the Public Accounts Committee, raised concerns about these delays and the impact on families.
 She said: "The changes made by the government will bring relief to many families experiencing the loss of a loved one.
 "No bereaved family should face unexpected tax charges because of delays outside their control.

 "By removing the two-year deadline, the government is ensuring that beneficiaries are not unfairly penalised while waiting for death benefits to be processed."
 She highlighted that the reform is particularly important in rural areas, where slower postal services and limited digital connectivity can cause additional delays and uncertainty.
 However, Ms Gilmour expressed disappointment that the change will not apply retrospectively.
 She said: "This means that families, including those within Tiverton and Minehead, who are affected by delays under previous rules will not receive the support they are desperate for.
 The minister for pensions confirmed pension scheme trustees and administrators will still be required to identify beneficiaries and process payments "without unnecessary delay."
 Ms Gilmour said it is crucial that families are treated with "empathy and fairness" and that the government should recognise there are still people in need of answers and support.
